oC.role: secondary/exactness: Q0 + B's 16 fresh points, combined

pC.role: baseline: the combined producer's probe loop (lift_scan + Feistel order, claude/n83-combined)

pP.role: candidate: combined + software-pipelined root-table probes with prefetch

pPaa.role: A/A control: a second candidate arm

pX.role: planted positive control: the candidate plus one discarded full-scan canonicalization per partner (claude/n83-combined's planted control), so its probes and relation are pP's and its time is known to be larger

rT.role: A's tuned rho (Fold/64/DP6, crypto 770f6a69; reconcile rT770), the strongest one-target rho measured at n=83; one process per primary point; gap reference and scalar cross-check

current_baseline: the combined producer, claude/n83-combined @ 88e1929fb (protocol frozen, run 38803625711 in flight when this protocol froze; its result is not used here). The baseline arm pC is that producer's probe loop byte for byte (make_online_source.py checks the combined derivation against its frozen digest and leaves scan_state128 unchanged); it runs in the same binary and job as the candidate.

decision_rule.invalid: any gate, identity check or control fails, or any primary point lacks a valid row in any of the four IC arms or the tuned rho: no verdict; every row is preserved
decision_rule.primary: improvement iff the 95% lower bound of R_m exceeds 1; regression iff its upper bound is below 1; otherwise not_separated
decision_rule.ratchet: a primary improvement makes combined + probe pipeline the new n=83 one-target baseline, recorded with R_m, R_g, the S_rho delta and the tuned-rho gap
decision_rule.scope: Tier 1 instance scope, one runner. Not a claim to beat rho: the tuned-rho gap is distance remaining.
decision_rule.secondaries: R_g, the slice bootstrap and the Q0 + 16 fresh block are reported; they never change the primary verdict or the ratchet

design.host: one fresh GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 runner (Tier 1 instance scope); every run one process pinned to one execution CPU (minimum of the affinity mask), clean environment, RAYON/KIC threads 1; all arms interleaved in one job; THP as the runner sets it (recorded)
design.process_model: each IC arm is one process per 64-point slice (17 for O): setup (index build, table load and verification, bijection self-test) once, then each target with its own one-target online interval and no target-dependent work shared between targets
design.runtime_estimate: build+tests 20-30 min; log-table check ~2 min; P: 4 x (30-35 s setup + 64 x 0.2-0.6 s) + 64 rho x 1-3 s = 5-9 min per slice, 6 slices 30-55 min; O: 2 x 1-2 min; diagnostic profiler ~2 min; total about 1.0-1.6 h (run 38786433493: IC setup 29-31 s per process, tuned rho 0.4-3.4 s per process)
design.within_segment_order: make_schedule.py's seeded shuffles (P: 2026103100 + s over the four IC processes and the 64 rho runs; O: 2026103300 + b)

gates: isolated_bench Tier 1 counters per run: exit 0, no timeout, verified=1, binary digest unchanged, no memory events; contention flags recorded and reported, never used to drop rows

every IC process: verified cached table on the frozen base, 29,880,000 states, the requested canonicalizer, order and probe pipeline reported in summary and every record, no start override, Feistel bijection self-test passed, full-scan index build, five phases sum to each online interval, setup ends before the first online interval
primary exactness on every point: pC, pP, pPaa and pX have identical probes and relation
one scalar per primary point across all four IC arms and the tuned rho; every scalar replays as [d]G = Q in the pinned oracle
Q0 + 16 fresh: oC and oP reproduce the archived Feistel probes and relation (run 38786433493's), scalars equal the archived ones and replay; Q0 equals the validation sidecar
multiplicity: one primary statistic; controls are pass/fail gates; secondaries are reported, never decide

online.factor_log_table_policy: B's archived table; re-verified before any timing by ../koblitz-n83-reconcile-20261014/verify_log_table.py in the pinned pure-Python oracle; every IC process additionally verifies all [L_j]G = R_j before target work
online.online_interval: producer's own clock: target_query_begin .. recovery_check_end, five exclusive phases; the Feistel order, the canonicalizer and the probe pipeline run inside the interval; index build, log-table load and verification, the order's bijection self-test and process launch are outside
online.primary_targets_file: inputs/primary_targets.json (make_targets.py; role probepipe-primary-v1, seeds 0..383; new role, no scalar known, disjoint from Q0, the 16 fresh points, the 384 scan-order held-out points and the 576 combined primary points)

power.population: the 384 old held-out targets' measured Feistel full-scan online times (run 38786433493) over the mean measured full / lift_scan ratio (run 38776966036), inputs/power_prior.json; per-point effect spread from the 16 lift_scan ratios; noise sigma 0.02 per target and 0.01 per process
power.rule: power - 2 * sqrt(power * (1 - power) / trials) >= 0.80 in the 1.03 scenario; then at least the design floor of 384 points

profile.status: diagnostic, cloud-agent VM; chose the fix, is not evidence of a speedup
profile.summary: diagnostic, VM: lookup 276 ns/probe (59% of 472) but 22 instructions; root solve 130 ns (28%); canonicalization 52 ns (11%); conversion 16 ns (3%); rest -2 ns. The lookup is latency-bound: few instructions, most of the time. Prefetch-pipelining the state's probes cut the in-situ lookup to 145 ns/probe in the profiler.

question: On the combined n=83 a=1 K600 one-target IC (lift_scan + Feistel order), does software-pipelining the root-table probes of each index state (compute all of the state's canonical keys, prefetch every key's home slot, then look them up in the same order) lower the one-target online time on new public points, with probes, relation and scalar unchanged?

statistics.S: S_rho = (mean IC online ms / tuned-rho ms per walk step) / sqrt(r), ms per step = median over all rT runs of online_ms / walk_steps; S_probe = mean probes / sqrt(r); for pC and pP, with the delta pP - pC
statistics.aa: pP / pPaa, ratio of means, seed 2026103530
statistics.also_reported: R_g = gm pC / gm pP (paired geometric mean, seed 2026103501); probe ratio; per-arm summaries, ns/probe and mean probes / law; R_m bootstrapped over the 64-point slices and per slice (sensitivity, seed 2026103550)
statistics.bootstrap: random.Random(seed); 10,000 resamples with replacement of the primary points; sorted; 95% interval = indices 250 and 9749
statistics.planted: pX / pP, ratio of means, seed 2026103532
statistics.primary: R_m = mean pC / mean pP, online_ms over all 384 primary points, seed 2026103500
statistics.rho_gap: tuned rho / IC for pC and pP on the same primary points, means and geometric means (seeds 2026103560-2026103563)
statistics.secondaries: Q0 + 16 fresh: oC / oP on the 16 fresh points (seed 2026103610) and Q0's two times

success_criterion: AGENTS.md 'Success criterion: iterative improvement of the index-calculus baseline': a verified, measured improvement over the current IC baseline under a protocol frozen before timing; each landed improvement becomes the new baseline with its delta.
